articles.headline: Rams WR Puka Nacua leaves practice with calf injury
articles.description: Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua left Thursday's practice with a calf injury, a team spokesperson said.
articles.headlineJa: ラムズのWRプカ・ナクア、ふくらはぎの負傷で練習を離脱
articles.descriptionJa: ロサンゼルス・ラムズのワイドレシーバー、プカ・ナクアが木曜日の練習中にふくらはぎの負傷により離脱したと、チームの広報担当者が発表した。
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua left Thursday's practice with a calf injury, a team spokesperson said.

Nacua was listed on the injury report as a limited participant in Thursday's practice.

The Rams were already without wide receiver Davante Adams, who injured his hamstring in Los Angeles' Week 6 loss to the Arizona Cardinals. Adams will miss six to 10 weeks with the injury, head coach Sean McVay said on Monday.

Nacua missed the Rams' Week 2 and 3 games with a psoas injury. In four games this season, Nacua has 37 catches for 417 yards and a touchdown.

Nacua is the latest in a long list of injury updates this week. Along with Adams, the Rams are without nose tackle Poona Ford, who will miss the rest of the season with a ruptured triceps, and defensive tackle Kobie Turner, who will miss "a handful of weeks" with a groin injury. The Rams also lost kicker Blake Grupe to a torn ACL in Week 6.

Outside of Nacua and Adams, the Rams have wide receivers Konata Mumpfield, Jordan Whittington, Tutu Atwell, CJ Daniels and Alex Bachman on their roster.

articles.headline: Source: Several teams interested in Colts RB Taylor as trade deadline approaches
articles.description: As the Colts plot their next moves after firing GM Chris Ballard, a source told ESPN that several teams would be open to a potential trade for Jonathan Taylor.
articles.headlineJa: 情報筋：トレード期限が迫る中、コルツのRBテイラーに関心を示す複数のチーム
articles.descriptionJa: コルツがクリス・バラードGMの解任を受けて次なる動きを模索する中、ジョナサン・テイラーのトレードについて、複数のチームが検討の余地があることをESPNに語ったと情報筋が伝えている。
articles.body:
INDIANAPOLIS -- Multiple teams would be open to a potential trade for Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor, a source told ESPN on Thursday, but it remains unclear whether the Colts are ready to unload players before the trade deadline.

The Colts are still plotting their next moves after Monday's firing of general manager Chris Ballard, with many around the NFL expected to gauge the team's interest in dealing some of its key players.

Taylor, the league's active leader in rushing yards per game (89.9), wasn't ready to broach the idea when asked Thursday.

"I haven't given any thought," he said when asked about his future. "That'd be crazy right now, especially because we've got a great Minnesota Vikings team that we have to go against. I think it would be a discredit and a disservice to my teammates and this whole organization to think about what could, what should, what may be."

Taylor was a 2020 draft pick of Ballard, who went on to sign Taylor to two contract extensions. The most recent, a three-year deal, was signed in August. But depending on how the weeks between now and the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline play out, the Colts (2-4) might be inclined to consider offers for their key talents. Indianapolis faces Minnesota and Jacksonville, which have a combined 9-2 record, in its next two games. 

The 2026 season was considered a pivotal one for the franchise after owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon put Ballard and coach Shane Steichen on notice that progress was expected after the disappointments of last season. It is widely expected that significant organizational changes might be coming after the eventual hire of a new GM.

Taylor, 27, ranks second to Baltimore's Derrick Henry in rushing yards since entering the league with 8,090 career yards. He has 492 rushing yards and seven rushing touchdowns in six games this season.

Defensive tackle DeForest Buckner, 32, is another player around whom trade speculation is swirling. Like Taylor, he declined to engage in the speculation on Thursday, saying, "I know how it works. But it's just distractions right now."

But when asked how he might react if a potential trade materialized, the 2020 first-team All-Pro didn't squash the idea.

"We'll see," said Buckner, who is scheduled to be a free agent after the season. "If that happens, we'll see how it goes."

All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson is in the final year of his deal and might be of interest to teams looking to make a postseason push. He reiterated on Wednesday his affinity for Indianapolis and the Colts organization.

Ballard was in his 10th season with the Colts and in the final year of his current contract. He was dismissed the morning after the Colts lost to the previously winless Tennessee Titans at Lucas Oil Stadium on Sunday. The loss, which came after the Colts gave up a 13-point lead, prompted loud booing and chants of "Fire Ballard!" from the home crowd.

articles.headline: Co-defendant denies Billups gave him info, pleads guilty in NBA gambling case
articles.description: Eric Earnest pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit wire fraud Thursday but denied receiving inside information from former NBA player and coach Chauncey Billups.
articles.headlineJa: NBA賭博事件の共同被告、ビルアップスからの情報提供を否定し罪を認める
articles.descriptionJa: エリック・アーネストは木曜日、電子詐欺共謀罪について罪を認めたが、元NBA選手でコーチのチャンシー・ビルアップスから内部情報を受け取ったことは否定した。
articles.body:
BROOKLYN, N.Y. -- Eric Earnest, a key co-conspirator in the inside information gambling case involving NBA player Terry Rozier, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit wire fraud in federal court Thursday, but his attorney said after the hearing that his client did not receive inside information from former NBA player and head coach Chauncey Billups.

Federal authorities alleged in the indictment that an unnamed co-conspirator told Earnest that the Portland Trail Blazers would be tanking and that certain Portland players would not play before a March 24, 2023, game against the Chicago Bulls. The co-conspirator was described in the indictment as an Oregon resident who was "an NBA player from approximately 1997 through 2014, and an NBA coach since at least 2021," details that align with Billups' career.

During his plea hearing, Earnest, 54, told the court that he "agreed with another person to place an illegal bet on an NBA game with a sportsbook" around March 24, 2023.

Assistant U.S. attorney David Berman said the government would have proved the co-conspirator was an NBA head coach at the time of the wager and had given inside information to others who bet on an NBA game. Berman did not name the co-conspirator, who was not charged in the case.

But after the hearing, Earnest's attorney, Peter Brill, told reporters, "Our position is that Chauncey Billups did not at any time provide inside information to Mr. Earnest that he used to place any bets."

Brill described the allegation that Billups had provided Earnest with the information as a "fundamental disagreement" with the government.

Billups' attorney, Marc Mukasey, told ESPN on Thursday afternoon he had no comment about Brill's statement. Billups was not charged in the inside information case.

In a separate hearing Thursday, Earnest also pleaded guilty to wire fraud in a case involving allegedly rigged poker games in which Billups was charged. Billups has pleaded not guilty.

Earnest admitted to playing in poker games that "were rigged against certain players" beginning in April 2019. Federal prosecutor Michael Gibaldi told the court he was prepared to show Earnest participated in games with shuffling machines that could help predict the hands of players at the table. That information would then be communicated to those allegedly involved in cheating.

Earnest could receive a maximum of 20 years in prison and three years of supervised release for each count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud along with maximum fines of $250,000 or double the gross gain or loss.

Prosecutors estimated based on federal sentencing guidelines that Earnest could face a sentence of 30 to 37 months in prison for the inside information case and 63 to 78 months for the poker case.

Earnest is scheduled for sentencing in the poker games case on March 4, 2027, and the inside information case on April 15, 2027. The remaining defendants in the two cases, including Rozier and Billups, are scheduled for trial in early 2027.

articles.headline: NFL Week 7 uniforms: Alternates galore as Texans go battle red, Lions all-black
articles.description: Here's a look at what each NFL team is wearing in Week 7, led by alternate looks from Houston, Detroit and Dallas.
articles.headlineJa: NFL第7週のユニフォーム：テキサンズのバトルレッドやライオンズのオールブラックなど、多彩なオルタネートが登場
articles.descriptionJa: ヒューストン、デトロイト、ダラスのオルタネート仕様を中心に、NFL各チームが第7週に着用するユニフォームを紹介する。
articles.body:
The throwbacks were well-represented in Week 6 of the NFL slate. While that's still the case this week, it's the alternates that lead the way -- including two monochromatic looks from the Houston Texans and Detroit Lions.

Houston will be wearing its "battle red" combination, which the team first unveiled in 2024. It's all red from head to toe complete with a similarly colored matte lid that includes a new bullhorn logo. The numbers are deep steel blue with a liberty white trim, while the red pants boast blue and white stripes. The New York Giants will counter with all-white. 

Also unveiled in 2024, the Lions are rocking their all-black threads against the Green Bay Packers. The black jersey and pants include a Honolulu Blue matte helmet with leaping Lions logo in silver. There's also a black stripe across the middle. Detroit first wore black uniforms in 1948 before bringing it back in 2005 as an alternate. The team stopped wearing them after the 2007 season before returning it in 2024. 

The Dallas Cowboys will don their color rush look against the Philadelphia Eagles on "Monday Night Football." Dallas unveiled these threads in 2015 with a silver helmet before an arctic white one debuted in 2022. The all-white combination has navy blue numbers and on the shoulder for a neat look.

Though alternates are the headliners, fans of the classics aren't leaving empty handed either in Week 7.

The Seattle Seahawks are wearing their throwbacks from the 1990s, complete with royal blue jerseys and silver pants and helmet. Seattle wore them last week on "Thursday Night Football." For the first time this season, the Atlanta Falcons and New York Jets are rocking classic uniforms. New York's is appropriately named "The Classic," and the all-white look pays homage to the 1968 championship season. It also includes uniform details from 1998 to 2018. Atlanta's threads include its iconic red helmet, which dates back to the 1960s, with black jerseys and white pants.

articles.body:
Week 7 brings another chance for NFL players to turn the pregame walkway tunnel into their own runway.

The New England Patriots visit the Chicago Bears on "Thursday Night Football," with temperatures around 60 degrees giving jackets and knits room to shine. Elsewhere, Sunday's forecast calls for temperatures in the low 70s in Nashville, leaving plenty of opportunity for lighter looks. Seattle offers more reason to layer up, with temperatures in the mid-50s and a slight chance of rain, while Philadelphia's Monday night forecast calls for temperatures in the upper 50s.

From relaxed fits to fall textures and tailored statements, players have plenty of ways to dress for the occasion. Here's a look at the best arrivals from Week 7.

Thursday's looks

Caleb Williams kept it sharp ahead of "Thursday Night Football," pairing a navy suit with a black crewneck shirt. The Chicago Bears quarterback skipped the tie but not the wired earbuds. Naturally, he had his matcha drink in one hand and a structured brown leather bag in the other.

articles.headline: The Broncos' defense has carried the team. Now QB Bo Nix wants to shoulder the load vs. Cardinals
articles.description: — Denver's ball-hawking defense has made it one of the better NFL teams so far this season.
articles.body:
GLENDALE, Ariz. -- — Denver's ball-hawking defense has made it one of the better NFL teams so far this season.


              Now the Broncos hope quarterback Bo Nix and the rest of the offense will start producing so they can truly become one of the league's elite.


              The Broncos (4-2) travel to face the Arizona Cardinals (2-4) on Sunday with questions about their offense, particularly Nix, who has underwhelmed in his third season as the team's quarterback. The 26-year-old has thrown for 1,049 yards and six touchdowns while completing 60.3% of his passes — which are all on track to be career lows.


              Broncos coach Sean Payton put some of Nix's problems on himself, saying he has to provide a better gameplan and leadership as each game unfolds.


              “I think he’s seen a lot," Payton said of Nix. "I shared this with you guys, and I’ll say it again: I have to be better just relative to in the course of the game. Each game takes on a different feel or style, if you will. Collectively, I think his play will be a byproduct of all of us doing our jobs better.”


              Nix threw for just 107 yards in last week's 17-14 overtime win against the Seahawks. The quarterback appreciated Payton shouldering some of the blame, but added that he has to do his part as well.


              “He’s been a really good leader right now," Nix said. “We need that. I think it goes back to us. I have to play better. We have to play better. The offense has to play better. He’s going to take his (blame) and that’s what great leaders do. I feel like I can overcome some of the stuff that is putting us in a bad spot, and I feel like I can play better.”


              The Cardinals snapped a four-game losing streak last week with a surprising 18-16 road win over the Los Angeles Rams. Arizona's defense was aggressive in its best performance of the season and Chad Ryland kicked six field goals, including the 43-yard game winner as time expired.


              Arizona is trying to snap a nine-game home losing streak that's lasted more than a calendar year.


              Quarterback Jacoby Brissett said it was good to get back in the win column against the Rams, but referenced one of first-year coach Mike LaFleur's favorite sayings: “Humility is a week away.”


              “He said that after the game and I think that applies so much because the Broncos don’t care what we did last week and we don’t either,” Brissett said. "It’s finding a way to go 1-0 this week.”


              Need to know
              Denver (4-2) at Arizona (2-4).


              When/where to watch: Sunday, 4:05 p.m. EDT, CBS


              Latest odds: Broncos by 4 1/2.


              Against the spread: Broncos 4-2; Cardinals 3-3.


              Last week: Broncos beat Seahawks 17-14 in OT; Cardinals beat Rams 18-16


              Last meeting: Broncos beat Cardinals 24-15 on Dec. 18, 2022, in Denver.


              Series record: Bronc

articles.headline: President Trump criticizes 76ers' LeBron James for actions amid national anthem
articles.description: President Donald Trump has accused LeBron James of disrespecting the U.S. after the 76ers star appeared to continue his warmups during the national anthem.
articles.headlineJa: トランプ大統領、国歌演奏中の行動について76ersのレブロン・ジェームズを批判
articles.descriptionJa: ドナルド・トランプ大統領は、76ersのスター選手であるレブロン・ジェームズが国歌演奏中にウォーミングアップを続けていたように見えたとして、米国を軽視していると非難した。
articles.body:
President Donald Trump on Thursday accused LeBron James of disrespecting the United States after the 76ers star appeared to continue his warmups while the national anthem was performed before Philadelphia's season opener Tuesday against the Knicks in New York.

James appeared to practice a golf swing and jump shot during The Star-Spangled Banner at Madison Square Garden. James, in his debut for the 76ers, was lined up alongside teammates who mostly stood still during the anthem.

"I said right from the beginning that he's no good, a TOTAL DISGRACE," Trump said of James in a social media post sharing the video. "LeBron James should apologize to all of those Great American Warriors and Heroes who died for the American Flag, and all that our Country stands for!"

Representatives for the 41-year-old James did not respond to requests for comment from ESPN. James, in his record 24th NBA season, was set to make his home debut for the Sixers on Thursday night against Cleveland.

Trump and James have been critical of each other for years, occasionally trading public swipes. 

Trump himself also has been criticized for his actions during the national anthem. In 2020, the Miami Herald posted a video of Trump waving his hands as if to conduct an orchestra while the national anthem was played at a Super Bowl watch party. In the brief video clip, Trump also appeared to gesture at others as those around him stood with hand over heart while the anthem was played. 

Information from ESPN's Dave McMenamin and The Associated Press was used in this report.

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Arsenal want £55M in any Gyökeres deal
articles.description: Arsenal has set their valuation for Viktor Gyökeres' transfer fee if the striker does depart in the next year. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Arsenal want £55 million in any potential deal for striker Viktor Gyökeres. Meanwhile, Manchester United are considering refreshing their back four, with three senior defender's contracts up at the end of the season.

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- If Viktor Gyökeres does leave Arsenal in the next year, then the North London club has set a valuation of £55 million on a potential exit, reports Football Insider. That is the same amount as the initial fee the Gunners paid Sporting CP to land the striker last summer. However, after a slow start to the current campaign, the Sweden international continues to be linked with a possible move away. Clubs in Italy, Spain, and elsewhere in England are keeping track of the situation, should the 28-year-old become available.

- Harry Maguire, Luke Shaw, and Lisandro Martínez are playing for their futures at Old Trafford, with their contracts due to expire next summer. That's according to according to TEAMtalk, which claims that United are not rushing to make a decision on the three defenders. That comes as preparations are being put in place for potential defensive reinforcements in 2027, with center back and left back set to be the main areas of consideration.

- Chelsea are showing interest in a move for Brighton midfielder Yasin Ayari, claims TEAMtalk. The 23-year-old Sweden international is in talks with the Seagulls over a contract extension, with his deal expiring in the summer, though the club has the option to extend it by a further year. However, while there are hopes of sealing a long-term stay with the club, talks have stalled over an improved contract. That has brought Chelsea into the conversation, with the Blues eyeing another swoop on Brighton, while Turkish Super Lig side Galatasaray are also monitoring the situation.

- Arsenal are among a group of teams following a potential switch for Monza striker Gustavo Varela. That's according to Mundo Deportivo, which claims that the Gunners are joined by Napoli and the 21-year-old's former club, Benfica, in keeping track of his progress. Varela has scored eight goals in seven matches across all competitions for Monza, making an impressive start with his new club. While Benfica is keen on a return, there is no clause that could guarantee a move back to Portugal, though there is a clause that will allow for the club to match an offer accepted from another club. However, with Arsenal and Napoli in the mix, that prospect has been described as difficult.

- Liverpool are in no rush to engage in conversations with Alexis Mac Allister over a new contract, despite the player voicing his disappointment at the lack of an offer earlier this season. That's according to The Telegraph, which claims that the Reds are yet to open talks, as the Argentina international has entered the final two years of his deal at Anfield. articles.headline: Wayne Rooney: Bruno Fernandes, Man United players acting like 'babies'
articles.description: Wayne Rooney has lambasted Manchester United's squad for acting like "babies" and urged Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez to look in the mirror.
articles.headlineJa: ウェイン・ルーニー：ブルーノ・フェルナンデスとマン・ユナイテッドの選手たちは「赤ん坊」のように振る舞っている
articles.descriptionJa: ウェイン・ルーニーは、マンチェスター・ユナイテッドのチームが「赤ん坊」のように振る舞っていると猛烈に批判し、ブルーノ・フェルナンデスとリサンドロ・マルティネスに自省を促した。
articles.body:
Wayne Rooney has lambasted Manchester United's squad for acting like "babies" and urged Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez to look in the mirror.

Fernandes followed Martínez in producing an eye-catching post-match interview on the back of Wednesday's 4-1 defeat at Como in the Champions League.

The result increased the scrutiny on Michael Carrick, who then faced criticism from Fernandes for the game plan in Italy but Rooney has accused the current United captain and Martínez -- who pointed the finger at Jason Wilcox -- of being selfish.

Sources: Carrick to lead Man United against Bournemouth

During an appearance on "The United Stand" podcast, Rooney, who also called for the board to provide clarity regarding Carrick's future, said: "When Martínez came out, I said this is an absolute nightmare because it will rip the dressing room apart. That was the start.

"We've seen it now with Bruno and you're going to see it with more players. The reason why is because them players don't want to take responsibility.

"You can say whether Bruno was right or wrong in what he said, but you have to take responsibility on the pitch, you have to take responsibility as a group of players and there were times when me and Sir Alex Ferguson wouldn't talk, but I'd run through a brick wall for him on the pitch.

"These players, they're selfish. They care about themselves, they don't care about their team-mates, don't care about the manager, about the staff or the fans, they care about themselves.

"If they're not getting what's right for them. They're like babies and just throw their toys out of the pram and go and deflect the blame on to anyone else but themselves. They have to look at themselves.

- Ogden: Who's to blame for Man United mess: Carrick, the players ... Ratcliffe?

- Dawson: Man United were abysmal in Como, but only Carrick who will suffer

"Bruno, he's having probably the worst run of form he's had since he's been at the club and again, it's no coincidence he's putting pressure on someone else because he doesn't want to face it.

"If he looks at himself in the mirror, if Martínez looks at himself in the mirror, all the players... they'll find what is looking back at them is them and it's not good enough."

articles.headline: LaMelo Ball obviously traveled on way to 3-pointer, NBA refs confirm
articles.description: The association that represents NBA referees confirmed that LaMelo Ball took two steps too many and traveled in a widely seen clip from Wednesday night's win over Miami.
articles.headlineJa: ラメロ・ボールの3ポイントシュートへの動きは明らかにトラベリング、NBA審判団が確認
articles.descriptionJa: NBA審判を代表する協会は、水曜夜のマイアミ戦での勝利における広く拡散された映像の中で、ラメロ・ボールが2歩多く踏み出し、トラベリングを行ったことを認めた。
articles.body:
MIAMI -- Upon review, Minnesota's LaMelo Ball traveled.

Really, really traveled.

The association that represents NBA referees posted a clip from Wednesday night's game between the Timberwolves and the Miami Heat and clarified -- not that it needed much clarification -- that Ball indeed did commit a violation on his way to a 3-pointer in the second quarter of Minnesota's win.

"For everyone asking, 'how is this legal?' It's not!" the referees' union wrote in a post on X. "He gathers with his right foot on the floor and would be permitted two steps by rule (left-right). He takes four steps after gathering the ball and travels."

Even Ball's brother, seven-year NBA player Lonzo Ball, got the call right moments after the play.

"Travel lmaoooo," Lonzo Ball posted.

Told in an interview with ESPN after the game that his brother made the traveling call, LaMelo Ball -- who was making his Minnesota debut -- still insisted he didn't commit a violation.

"He hatin'. He hatin'," LaMelo Ball said in the televised interview. "See, I gotta give him a call right now, cause with the family, he knows what you're supposed to do. Even if I'm wrong, I'm right. That's how it goes."

Ball's shouldn't-have-counted shot broke what was a 39-39 tie at the time, but in the end it wasn't like the 3-pointer played a big role in the outcome. LaMelo Ball finished the game with 21 points, and Minnesota won 131-106.

articles.headline: Who's to blame for Man United mess: Carrick, the players ... Ratcliffe?
articles.description: The bitter truth about United is that their prolonged and deep-rooted decline can be attributed to much more than their manager. Who deserves the most blame, and why?
articles.headlineJa: マン・Uの混乱、責任は誰にあるのか：キャリック、選手たち……それともラトクリフ？
articles.descriptionJa: ユナイテッドに関する苦い真実は、その長期化し根深い衰退の原因は監督だけではないということだ。誰が最も責められるべきであり、その理由は何か？
articles.body:
Manchester United are in crisis -- again. One of the world's biggest football clubs is in the middle of its worst start to a season in 40 years and suffered their heaviest Champions League defeat since 1994 when losing 4-1 to Como this week, so who is to blame?

Is it the owners -- the Glazer family and Sir Jim Ratcliffe -- the senior executives, the manager or the players? The bitter truth about United is that their prolonged and deep-rooted decline can be attributed to all of the above.

So why does the blame lie in all areas, and what, if anything, can be done to drag United out of its doom spiral? ESPN has assessed United's problems and why nobody at Old Trafford can escape the scrutiny for the club's cycle of failure.

- Dawson: It's dire at Man United, but only Carrick will suffer

- UCL Talking Points: What to make of Man United's mess?

- Who are Como? The vacation-destination club that just rocked Man United

The Glazers

United have been owned by the Glazer family since 2005 following the completion of a controversial leveraged buyout.

The Glazers, who also own the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, purchased United for £790 million but borrowed £600 million, using the club as security for the loan, to complete the deal. As a consequence, the previously debt-free club was instantly plunged into £600m of debt.

That debt has been a millstone for United ever since and during the 21 years of Glazer ownership, over £1 billion has gone out of the club in debt repayments, accumulated interest, refinancing costs and dividends to shareholders. Every year of Glazer ownership has seen an average of £50m go out of the club on non-football costs -- a figure that could translate into a new signing or more attractive player wages.

Under the Glazers, Old Trafford has become a decaying stadium no longer fit for purpose and the team has suffered from long-term under-investment. Although the Glazers surrendered control of football operations to minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Feb 2024 -- a £1.25 billion pay-day for a 27.7% stake in the club -- the nine-year period Sir Alex Ferguson's retirement as manager in 2013 and Ratcliffe's arrival was dominated by poor managerial and executive appointments by the Glazers and a woeful player recruitment record.

Everything that is going wrong at United can be traced back to the Glazers.

Percentage of blame: 50%

Sir Jim Ratcliffe

One of Britain's richest men and a lifelong United fan born less than 10 miles from Old Trafford, Ratcliffe was billed as the club's savior when he bought a 27.7% stake in exchange for control of football operations in February 2024.

He promised to overhaul the club, saying United's data analytics department was "last century," and he made an immediate impact by hiring Man City chief operating officer Omar Berrada as CEO and recruiting director football Dan Ashworth from Newcastle. Despite the early positive moves, Ratcliffe fired Ashworth less than six months in the job and has since lurched f

articles.headline: Erling Haaland set to return with Man City 'hungry' to continue perfect start
articles.description: Manchester City coach Enzo Maresca said Erling Haaland is available for Saturday's trip to Aston Villa, while three other players remain doubtful.
articles.body:
Manchester City coach Enzo Maresca said Erling Haaland is available to return for Saturday's trip to Aston Villa, while three other players remain doubtful.

Haaland, who has scored 12 goals in nine games to start to the season, remained on the bench throughout Man City's 5-1 Champions League thrashing of AEK Athens on Tuesday.

- Maresca determined to help Foden back to his best

- Walker: 'No intention' of removing Man City tattoos

- Football watchdog chair asserts 'absolute' power to force City sale

But Maresca confirmed Thursday that the Norway striker is in line to return, while Matheus Nunes, Nico O'Reilly and Mateo Kovacic had been improving as City prepare to visit Villa Park after three consecutive home games.

"We have a session this afternoon. [The injured players] can all be available or not in terms of still doubt," Maresca told a news conference. "Yesterday, they were all improving, and we'll see this afternoon. For sure, Erling is the only one 100% available."

City go into the game three points clear of champions Arsenal at the top of the Premier League, with Maresca having begun his first season in charge with seven straight league wins.

Despite the perfect start, the former Chelsea coach insisted the team is not resting on its laurels.

"The mood is very good," Maresca said. "I said many times the mood is good. We are happy with our start but we are more hungry for more wins. We're happy at the moment but want more.

"It's too early [to say teams are not in the title race]. Seven games, there are many games to go. It's too early."

As well as Haaland, Rayan Cherki has been another major contributor to the positive early weeks of Maresca's tenure. The France international has six goals and two assists thus far and Maresca praised Cherki as one of Europe's best players when deployed in the right areas.

"If we are able to keep him there, and if we are able to find him between the lines, so in the right position, I think he is one of the best player in Europe," Maresca said.

Information from The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.headline: In-the-dark Kane trying not to 'stress' over Monday's Ballon d'Or reveal
articles.description: Bayern striker Harry Kane said he would prefer to know ahead of time whether he has won the Ballon D'Or, adding he is still in the dark over Monday's decision.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane said he would prefer to know ahead of time whether he has won the Ballon D'Or, adding he is still in the dark over Monday's decision.

The 33-year-old is the bookmakers' favourite to become the first Englishman to win the coveted prize since Michael Owen in 2001, but he faces competition from Barcelona's Lamine Yamal and Inter Miami CF's Lionel Messi among others on the 30-man shortlist.

As of 2024, organisers France Football insist they do not warn the winners in advance. That did not stop Real Madrid boycotting the event that year upon learning via a leak that Vinícius Júnior had been overlooked in favour of Rodri.

Kane scored for the tenth consecutive Champions League game on Wednesday as Bayern Munich drew 2-2 with Arsenal at Allianz Arena. Only Cristiano Ronaldo (11) has a longer streak in the competition's history and speaking to reporters after the game, Kane said: "They want everyone to go, all the big names there and there will be more people watching it if they don't know, so I can understand why.

"I think my wife would prefer to know and my family, it's very stressful for everyone. From my point of view, of course, I'd love to know to just kind of see and not have to wait throughout the whole night. But it is their decision, I can't control that. We'll have to just enjoy it and try not to stress out too much.

"I try not to think about it. Obviously it is hard not to. There are always rum ours flying around and you try to stay away from it. We have important games today and I know we have another important one on Sunday before the event on Monday so that's where my focus is.

"Of course I am going to try and enjoy Monday night as much as possible. It is a big occasion so we will have to wait and see."

Bayern have drawn two and won once in the League Phase of the UCL so far, leaving them in 14th place in the table. The Bundesliga champions face third-place Freiburg on Sunday as they try to remain atop of Germany's top flight.
